header.running_head: The Justice of Hadhrat Umar Farooq (RA)

blocks.text:
Hadhrat Ubay (RA) and the two men took their case to him.
(After hearing the case,) Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "I do not see any way in which you can remove him from his house without his consent." Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Tell me whether you found this judgement in the Book of Allaah or in a Hadith of Rasulullaah ﷺ?" "It is in a Hadith of Rasulullaah ﷺ," replied Hadhrat Ubay (RA). When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked for substantiation, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that while Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) the son of Hadhrat Dawood (AS) was constructing Baytul Maqdas, he found the walls destroyed every morning after he had them built. Allaah then sent revelation telling him that he would be unable to build anything on the land of another person without the person's consent."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then left Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) and Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) himself included it in the Masjid at a later stage. [^1]
A Narration of Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib in this Regard

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once intended to take the house of Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) to include it in the Masjid. However, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) refused to hand the house over. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) resolved that he would certainly have possession of the house, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) proposed that they appoint Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) to pass judgement between them. Hadhrat Umar (RA) agreed and they both approached Hadhrat Ubay (RA). After they had related the matter to him, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said, "Allaah sent revelation to Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Dawood instructing him to construct the Baytul Maqdas. The land belonged to a man whom Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) approached to buy it from him. However, when Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) handed over the money to the man, he asked, 'Is this price that you are paying better or is that which you are taking from me better?' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) replied, 'Certainly that which I am taking from you is better.' 'In that case,' said the man, 'I shall not accept it.'
Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) then gave the man a higher price. The man then did the same thing two or three times until Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) made a condition with him, 'I am buying this land from you at the price you fix. You may therefore not ask me which of the two is better.' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) took the purchased land from him at the price he fixed, which happened to be twelve thousand Qintaar of gold (one Qintaar equals four thousand gold coins). Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) then felt that the amount was too big to give the man. Allaah then sent revelation to him saying, 'If you are paying him from something that is your own, then you know best (what you have to do). However, if you are paying him from what We have provided for you, then give him whatever he is pleased with.' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (AS) then paid the amount."
